The only reason I can think of here is that Age of Youngest Account is a FICO scoring factor. Thus, if you opened four cards in a two year period, each six months apart, that would guarantee that you constantly had a fairly low AoYA, whereas by opening them all at once your AoYA would become much higher sooner, There are many practical reasons not to open multiple cards on the same day, however — or the same week, same month, etc.

That’s a pretty nasty thing to say. Your choice not to ever pay an AF, but not your place to condemn the hundreds of thousands of intelligent and well-informed credit card users who come to a different conclusion after analyzing the benefit of the card versus its AF.
It’s not a question of how much money the CC companies make – it’s how much a consumer can make from using the CC benefit. For instance, when I got the Citi Prestige card for the first time a few years ago, the annual fee was $350. There was an annual travel credit of $250 per calendar year, so that was $500 during the first 12 months. There was and still is a fourth night free for EVERY hotel stay, with no annual limits. Also at that time, the hotel stays could be booked in a way which triggered loyalty points. Points earned on purchases could be cashed out at .0125. I do not ever carry a balance, so the interest rates don’t affect me.
